text:
morgan: Alert: noticed a sharp billing spike (~$14k) over the last 3h for us-west2 GPU pool. https://grafana.company/reports/abc123
kayla: got the cloud billing email too. looks like autoscaler fell back to an expensive flavor when preemptible pool was exhausted :grimacing:
alex: any autoscaler logs? could be preferred_types ordering or a label mismatch.
morgan: grabbing logs now. here's the autoscaler decision snippet:
```
Autoscaler: scale_up: reason=unschedulable_pods selected_instance=p4d.24xlarge pool=reserved-gpu available=0
```
deploy-bot: AutoscalerBot: launched 24 instances in us-west2-a (group=training-pool) at 2026-03-18T14:05:12Z
sre-ops: we merged terraform PR #1745 last night that changed module.provisioner.preferred_types: p4d was accidentally promoted to first-choice. that's why it picked that family.
kayla: right — our Reserved Commitment (contract RC-2025-usw2) only covers gtx-3xx family. p4d is fully on-demand and ~6-8x cost. need rollback and a guard.
alex: quick mitigation: 1) terraform rollback target module.provisioner.preferred_types 2) cordon new nodes and scale down gracefully
commands:
```
# roll back preferred types
terraform apply -target=module.provisioner -var 'preferred_types=["g4dn","a100"]'
# cordon
kubectl cordon node-xyz
kubectl drain node-xyz --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
```
morgan: rolling back now. started turning off 12 of the new instances; cloud console shows scale down in progress. estimate ~11k incremental cost already incurred.
billing-bot: BillingAlertBot: created INCIDENT-1342 for billing spike. estimated overage: $11,320. notifying @finance and @infra.
sre-ops: follow-ups: add CI check to block preferred_types reorder without an approval from infra, and add autoscaler policy to prefer committed families before on-demand. i'll own the remediation.
kayla: assigning postmortem to @kayla and @alex. we'll run a short retro and update runbook. :white_check_mark:
morgan: thanks everyone — i'll update the incident ticket with final numbers when available.
